findings.problem: `wassersteinEDist_dirac_left` is tagged `@[simp]`, but it takes the explicit hypothesis `hd : Measurable fun z : X × X ↦ edist z.1 z.2`. Mathlib's `measurable_edist` is not a simp lemma (it has no `@[simp]`, only a plain theorem). I found no simp lemma that proves `hd`, and it is not an instance argument. So simp most likely cannot discharge `hd`, and the attribute probably never fires. Every use I found passes `measurable_edist` by hand through `rw`, including the two reverse rewrites here. This proof expands `eLpNorm` back into `wassersteinEDist` by hand, which is the opposite of the simp direction. The `@[simp]` tag therefore gives a misleading interface: it suggests a normal form (Dirac Wasserstein distance becomes `eLpNorm`) that simp does not reliably produce when the measurability side condition is present.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one of these two options in Basic.lean. (a) Remove `@[simp]` from `wassersteinEDist_dirac_left`, since all uses are explicit `rw`. (b) Keep a real simp lemma by giving it a dischargeable context. For example, state a variant under `[SecondCountableTopology X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X]` that proves `hd` internally with `measurable_edist`, and tag that variant `@[simp]`. The plain version with `hd` stays untagged for general use. With (b), the Dirac-to-`eLpNorm` normal form is available to simp. This proof would then not need the two `rw [← …]` steps, and could rewrite the target with `simp only` or `rw` from the Wasserstein side.
findings.benefit: Readers are not misled by a simp attribute that cannot fire. The orientation of the lemma then matches how it is used here, instead of being undone by `rw ←` at each call site. If option (b) is taken, downstream proofs such as this one, `Moment.lean:177` and `CurvatureDimension.lean:128` can use simp-based normalisation instead of repeating `measurable_edist` by hand.
